title: Starting Point Check
purpose: Understand a new IT work-study student's starting knowledge, confidence level, and recommended training path.
student_intro: This is not pass/fail. Auto-scored questions help recommend a starting path; written answers are saved for mentor review so your mentor can support you.

role_alignment.title: Work Style and Support Needs
role_alignment.purpose: Help mentors understand which environment may help the student succeed fastest. This signal is separate from technical scoring.

signals.label: Technical troubleshooting interest
signals.description: Interest in investigating device, account, printer, monitor, or other technical issues.

signals.label: User-facing support interest
signals.description: Interest in greeting users, calming support interactions, and helping people find next steps.

signals.label: Process/documentation strength
signals.description: Comfort with checklists, accurate details, records, and clear mentor summaries.

signals.label: Handling unclear tasks
signals.description: Comfort stopping, clarifying, and continuing safely when a task is unclear.

signals.label: Asking for help
signals.description: Willingness to ask specific questions instead of guessing or waiting silently.

signals.label: Structured shadowing support
signals.description: Signal that the student may benefit from observation, closer check-ins, or more role exploration before placement.

recommendations.label: IT Launchpad
recommendations.summary: Student appears interested in technical troubleshooting and shows safe beginner habits. Begin with IT foundations, hardware basics, escalation rules, and mentor-supervised tasks.
next_steps: Begin the recommended IT training path.
Use hardware basics, escalation rules, and mentor-supervised beginner tasks as early practice.

recommendations.label: Hybrid IT/User Support
recommendations.summary: Student may benefit from supervised IT exposure while also using communication strengths in user-facing support. Begin with shadowing, documentation practice, and structured beginner-safe IT tasks.
next_steps: Pair IT shadowing with user-facing support observation.
Practice documentation, greeting users, and beginner-safe checks with mentor review.

recommendations.label: Student Services Exploration
recommendations.summary: Student shows stronger current alignment with user-facing process support than technical troubleshooting. Admissions, Advising, front desk support, or another structured student services role may match the student's current strengths.
next_steps: Explore Admissions, Advising, front desk, or related student services workflows.
Use communication, process guidance, and structured support strengths while continuing role discovery.

recommendations.label: Structured Shadowing
recommendations.summary: Student may benefit from observing IT, Admissions, and Advising workflows before final placement. Focus on confidence, communication, and task preference discovery.
next_steps: Schedule structured observation across IT and student services environments.
Review confidence, communication, and task preferences before final placement.

questions.prompt: Have you worked in an IT, computer lab, help desk, repair, or tech support role before?
Which of these have you done before? Select all that apply.

options.label: Worked with inventory or asset tags

questions.prompt: What are you most nervous about in this role?
review_rubric: Names a real concern or support need honestly.
Gives the mentor useful context for the first check-in.
Uses safe language instead of pretending to know more than they do.
questions.mentor_use: Use this answer to identify early support needs and confidence concerns.

sections.title: Confidence
sections.intro: Use 1 = Not confident and 5 = Very confident.

questions.prompt: How confident do you feel using computers in general?
How confident do you feel troubleshooting basic computer problems?
How confident do you feel asking for help when you are stuck?
How confident do you feel reading step-by-step technical documentation?
In a school or workplace IT environment, what is a domain?

options.label: A managed network environment used for accounts, computers, and access

questions.explanation: In this context, a domain helps an organization manage user accounts, computers, permissions, and access in a central way.

questions.prompt: What does computer imaging mean?

options.label: Taking a picture of a computer
Preparing a computer with the required operating system, software, and settings

questions.explanation: Computer imaging prepares a computer with the standard operating system, software, settings, and configuration it needs before being used.

questions.prompt: SCCM or Configuration Manager is generally used for what?

options.label: Managing and deploying software, updates, and operating systems

questions.explanation: Configuration Manager is commonly used to manage computers, deploy software, run updates, and support imaging.

questions.prompt: What is a ticket?

options.label: A record of a request, issue, task, or support interaction

questions.explanation: A ticket is a record of work that needs to be done or support that was provided.

questions.prompt: What is an asset tag?

options.label: A label or ID used to track equipment

questions.explanation: An asset tag is used to identify and track equipment such as computers, monitors, printers, and other technology.

questions.prompt: A monitor says "No Signal." What should you check first?

options.label: Check power, display cable, monitor input/source, and whether the computer is on

questions.explanation: A No Signal message is often related to power, cabling, monitor input/source, or whether the computer is sending video.

questions.prompt: A keyboard is not working. What is a beginner-safe first step?

options.label: Check the connection or try a known-working keyboard

questions.explanation: Checking the connection or testing with a known-working keyboard is a safe first step when approved by the department.

questions.prompt: Which of these is usually beginner-safe?

options.label: Checking whether a monitor cable is connected

questions.explanation: Checking a cable connection is usually safe. Guessing, changing settings, or deleting files can cause problems.

questions.prompt: A computer is running slowly. What is the safest beginner response?

options.label: Delete files until the computer is faster
Document the symptoms, ask what the user was doing, and check beginner-safe items if instructed
Ignore the issue because slow computers are normal

questions.explanation: The safest beginner response is to collect basic context, perform only approved beginner-safe checks, and escalate when needed.

questions.prompt: You are asked to help image a computer, but you are not sure which image or workflow to use. What should you do?

options.label: Pick the one that seems closest
Stop and ask your mentor or the IT tech on duty

questions.explanation: A new work-study student should not guess during imaging.

questions.prompt: You see an unfamiliar error while helping with a computer. What should you do?

options.label: Restart the process repeatedly without telling anyone
Document the error and ask your mentor

questions.explanation: Unfamiliar errors should be documented and escalated.

questions.prompt: A user asks you a question and you do not know the answer. What should you do?

options.label: Ask your mentor or supervisor and document the question if needed

questions.explanation: It is better to ask for help than to guess.

questions.prompt: What should good ticket notes or mentor summaries include?

options.label: The issue, what was checked, what happened, and what still needs to be done
Nothing unless the issue is serious

questions.explanation: Good summaries explain the issue, checks, result, and what still needs to happen.

sections.title: Work Style and Support Needs
sections.intro: These questions are separate from technical scoring. They help your mentor understand which environment may help you learn and contribute safely.

questions.prompt: You are given a task, but one step is unclear. What would you most likely do?

options.label: Guess and keep going so I do not slow anyone down
Stop and ask a specific clarification question
Wait silently until someone checks on me

questions.prompt: A user is frustrated and says, "IT never fixes anything." What is the best beginner-safe response?

options.label: Tell them another IT person probably forgot
Promise the issue will be fixed today
Stay calm, avoid blame, and tell them you will check with your mentor

questions.prompt: Which type of work sounds most interesting to you?

options.label: Figuring out why a computer, monitor, printer, or account is not working
Helping students or users understand a process, form, appointment, or next step
Organizing information, checking records, and making sure details are correct

questions.prompt: Which task would you feel most comfortable learning first?

options.label: Checking cables, asset tags, device names, and error messages
Greeting students or users and helping direct them to the right person
Reviewing a checklist and making sure each step is complete
Watching someone else first before choosing

questions.prompt: A mentor asks you to document what happened during a task. What would you include?

options.label: What I checked, what happened, and what I still need help with
My opinion about who caused the problem
Private information, just in case it helps

questions.prompt: Which situation sounds most stressful to you?

options.label: A computer problem where I do not know the answer yet
A frustrated person asking for help
A task with many small details that must be accurate
A quiet task where I have to work independently

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes you right now?

options.label: I want to learn technical troubleshooting, even if it feels challenging
I mostly want to help people navigate processes and get answers
I like organized tasks with clear steps and records
I am still exploring what kind of work fits me
